clue.text: South American ruler popular with Guatemala, etc.

parts.note: popular means in, as in fashionable
Guatemala and its neighbours make up Central America, abbreviated CA

explanation.surface: A ruler from South America who is well liked in Guatemala and nearby countries.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca was the emperor of the Andean empire centred on Peru.

clue.text: Contract for psychologist

definitions.meaning: second meaning: slang for a psychiatrist or therapist, short for headshrinker

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests signing a deal with a therapist; 'Contract' is a verb, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for getting smaller and informal slang for a therapist of the mind.

clue.text: Complain when buzzer is on loud

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, so the buzzer comes first

parts.note: a bee is an insect that buzzes
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling because a noisy buzzer has been left switched on.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef is informal slang for grumbling or making a complaint.

clue.text: Score century, possibly? Not in this game

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: Asking whether scoring a hundred is possible, then noting it never happens in this sport.
explanation.walkthrough: SCORE plus C rearranges to the answer; 'Not in this game' points out that nobody scores a century in football, unlike cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is association football, the game the clue says centuries do not occur in.

clue.text: Only half fared well in guest house

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, so the answer is concealed inside them

explanation.surface: Only half the visitors had a pleasant stay at the guest house.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'fareD WELL IN Guest'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling is any place where someone lives, a home or residence.

clue.text: Working group's statement of belief

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a body of people sharing an occupation
second meaning: a declaration of faith

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link; the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an occupation and those in it, and an open avowal of faith.

clue.text: Single member of team with limited facilities

parts.note: single means one
a team of horses pulls a cart, so one member is a horse

explanation.surface: One player in a side that has little in the way of equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-horse town is small and poorly provided, an idiom for lacking amenities.

clue.text: Discriminating, again imposed legal punishment

parts.note: RE is a prefix meaning again
fined means made to pay a penalty by a court

explanation.surface: A judge with fine judgement who has once more handed down a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined taste is cultivated and discerning, able to tell good from bad.

clue.text: Sister's in control here — keep going!

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: a ward sister is the senior nurse in charge on a hospital ward
second meaning: ... as a cry urging people forward

explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a Sister is the senior nurse running a ward, so where she is in charge is ON WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Onward is an exclamation of encouragement telling people to advance further.

clue.text: Charge resulting from quarrel about a ring-leader

indicators.note: about means going round, so the quarrel surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of ring

parts.note: supplies its first letter

explanation.surface: A fee that came out of a dispute concerning a ringleader.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a set charge or duty, such as a fare or import levy.

clue.text: Turned smooth, in reality, as result of cosmetic surgery

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the turned word sits within the word for reality

parts.note: fact means reality, what is true

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the word for smooth is read backwards

parts.note: to file is to smooth with a rasp

explanation.surface: Wrinkles actually smoothed away thanks to a cosmetic operation.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads like a description of the surgery, tempting a cryptic-definition reading, but only the last two words define; a file is a tool for smoothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A facelift is the operation that tightens facial skin to remove wrinkles.

clue.text: Task-oriented groups improperly taking power, sir?

indicators.note: improperly means the letters are put in the wrong order and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Committees accused of seizing control wrongly, with a question to their chairman.
explanation.definitionFit: These are committees set up to study and report on a specific problem.

clue.text: Like nine-year-old with extra width near middle?

definitions.text: Like nine-year-old with extra width near middle?

indicators.note: with extra says something is being added to the phrase for nine-year-old
near middle says the addition goes close to the centre of that phrase, inside it

parts.note: a nine-year-old is over eight

explanation.surface: A podgy child of nine with a thickened waistline.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a description of a plump child, which makes it nearly an &lit: the width letter lands just past the centre of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Overweight means heavier than is healthy, carrying extra bulk around the waist.

clue.text: In European city, is doing well on course?

parts.note: on a golf course, par is the expected standard score

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone in a European capital is getting on well in their studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests education but means a golf course, where par is the target score.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is the capital city of France.

clue.text: Rail timetable finally introduced for Paddington, say

indicators.note: introduced means brought inside, so the letter goes into the rail

parts.note: a rail is a bar

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of timetable

parts.note: supplies its last letter

explanation.surface: A railway timetable at last brought in for London's Paddington station.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington is a London rail terminus, but here it is Paddington Bear from the children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington is a famous fictional bear from Peru in Michael Bond's stories.

clue.text: Cartel on border in best position to observe fighting

definitions.text: in best position to observe fighting

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece is placed on top of the other

parts.note: a ring is a group of traders fixing prices, a cartel
a side is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A cartel operating at a frontier is ideally placed to watch combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringside seats are those closest to a boxing ring, giving the clearest view.

clue.text: Race in which neighbouring teams compete

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a famous flat horse race at Epsom
second meaning: a local ... is a match between clubs from the same area

explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is England's best-known horse race, run at Epsom; a local derby is a football match between nearby rival clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a classic horse race and a contest between local sporting rivals.

clue.text: Police with weapon that was used to punish mutineers

definitions.text: that was used to punish mutineers

parts.note: the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: Armed police with a weapon once used to discipline rebellious sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard, often just the Yard, is the Metropolitan Police headquarters in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutinous sailors were hanged from the yardarm, a spar on a ship's mast.

clue.text: Increase never painlessly achieved, so they say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rise or growth

definitions.text: never painlessly achieved, so they say

explanation.walkthrough: The second half alludes to the proverb 'no pain, no gain'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gain is a rise or increment, the reward the gym proverb says needs effort.

clue.text: Moving air is what this music producer needs

definitions.text: Moving air is what this music producer needs

parts.words: Moving air is what this music producer needs
parts.note: a music producer is read as something that makes music, sounded by blown breath

explanation.walkthrough: 'Music producer' suggests a record producer, but here it is something that produces sound when blown.
explanation.definitionFit: Flutes, oboes and trumpets sound only when a player blows breath through them.

clue.text: Relative gains by unions at work before left was corrupted

indicators.note: before means the first piece comes ahead of the rest

parts.note: in, as in 'in' the office, means at work

indicators.note: corrupted means spoilt or altered, so the letters of was are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pay rises won by trade unions in the workplace before the left went bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unions' suggests trade unions but means marriages, which is what makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Relatives by marriage are acquired when people wed, so unions here are marriages.

clue.text: Indian doctor, aggressive high-flier

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
a hawk is a bird of prey that flies high; also a warlike politician

explanation.surface: A doctor described as a combative high achiever.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mohawk are a Native American people of the Iroquois confederacy.

clue.text: Go to pieces in defeat, retreating in fall deliberately

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the reversed defeat goes inside the fall

parts.note: to dive is to fall on purpose, as a footballer feigning a foul

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a loss is a defeat

explanation.surface: A footballer collapsing after a loss, accused of throwing himself down on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: In football, a dive is a player falling deliberately to win a foul, which is the sense of 'fall deliberately'.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissolve is to break up or disintegrate, or to collapse emotionally.

clue.text: Odd bits of exam, say, not very challenging

indicators.note: odd bits means the first, third, fifth and seventh letters, the odd-numbered positions

parts.note: its odd letters, first and third, are E and A
its odd letters, first and third, are S and Y

explanation.surface: Parts of an exam, for instance, that are not too hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Something easy demands little effort and poses no real difficulty.

clue.text: Party games like this preferred by players?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an informal reception held in one's house

definitions.text: games like this preferred by players
definitions.meaning: second meaning: teams prefer matches played on their own ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Party games' looks like one phrase but splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a social gathering hosted in a house and matches played on a team's own ground.

clue.text: Unkind people hiding answer — one's covering end of clue

indicators.note: hiding says the word for people conceals the letter for answer within it

parts.note: a word for adult males, standing for people in general

explanation.surface: Cruel folk concealing a solution, with one hiding the final part of a clue.
explanation.walkthrough: A second route works too: 'one' is MAN, covering E, the end of 'clue', gives the same answer, so 'one's covering end of clue' confirms it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes someone spiteful or unkind as well as stingy.

clue.text: Follow performance with commercial break

indicators.note: break means interrupt, so the commercial splits the performance

parts.note: a show is a performance
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: Watch a TV show that is interrupted by an advertising break.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone is to tail them closely without being noticed.

clue.text: How teams changed, up to a point

indicators.note: changed means altered in arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Remarking on how much the sides have altered, at least partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat means to some extent or moderately, a partial degree.
